record.title: ANEEL approves Group A electricity-market migration and Open Energy rules
record.summary: ANEEL’s 27 October 2026 announcement says its board approved rule changes for Group A consumers in medium and high voltage and instituted Open Energy. The announcement describes a standardized, consent-based way to access and share consumption, billing and metering data, with an initial comparison page and standardized access due within 12 months of rule publication and API sharing within 24 months. For most simplified AS/A4 cases it reports migration deadlines falling from 180 to 90 days; other cases remain at 180 days. The signed resolutions and Official Gazette publication/effective dates were not retrieved in this check, and no adoption, electricity-price, procurement or data-platform outcome is established.
organizations: Câmara de Comercialização de Energia Elétrica (CCEE)

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: ANEEL published an official announcement dated 27 October 2026 saying its board approved rule changes for Group A electricity-market migration and instituted Open Energy.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: ANEEL says the measures standardize migration to the free-contracting market and provide consent-based access to and sharing of consumer consumption, billing and metering data; it describes staged functions due within 12 and 24 months after the rule is published.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: ANEEL says most simplified migration cases for AS/A4 units will have a regular deadline reduced from 180 to 90 days, while other units retain 180 days.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The signed resolutions, Official Gazette publication and effective dates were not retrieved in this check; consumer adoption, realized price or procurement effects, and operational performance of Open Energy are not established.

evidence_gaps.description: The signed final resolutions and corresponding Official Gazette publication/effective dates were not retrieved.
No implementation, migration adoption, market-price or API performance outcome is available in the inspected source.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented as ANEEL describes, standardized market migration and consent-based access to electricity-use data could affect procurement choices and market-information access for medium- and high-voltage consumers, including some large compute loads. The score reflects that potential consequence only; it does not establish realized savings, platform performance or adoption.
limitations: This evidence is ANEEL’s public announcement; signed resolutions and Official Gazette publication/effective dates were not inspected.
No actual migration, consumer uptake, electricity price effect, large-load procurement result, or Open Energy API operation was measured.
The announced timetable is measured from publication of the rule; without the resolution and publication date, calendar deadlines cannot be calculated.

technical.claimed_result: ANEEL says the approved rules will streamline Group A switching and institute phased Open Energy access and sharing.
technical.demonstrated_result: The regulator publicly announced the board approval and described the rule; implementation and outcomes are not established.
technical.mechanism: Standardized migration procedures and consent-based access to consumption, billing and metering data, with staged comparison and API functions.
technical.regime: Brazilian electricity consumers in Group A (medium/high voltage); Group B expansion remains a separate future regulatory process.
technical.reproducibility: The public agency announcement is accessible; the signed resolutions were not retrieved in this check.
technical.strongest_baseline: The announcement compares the simplified migration deadline for most AS/A4 cases with the prior 180-day process; no measured consumer or price comparison is reported.

brief.title: ANEEL approves Group A electricity-market migration and Open Energy rules
brief.why_it_matters: For medium- and high-voltage buyers, including some data-centre and compute operators, simpler switching and standardized access to consumption and pricing information could change procurement options. This is a regulatory design announcement, not evidence that consumers have switched, lowered costs or achieved working data portability.
